title: ‘The Odyssey’ Surpasses $700 Million Globally After 12 Days in Theaters
description: “The Odyssey” has surpassed $700 million at the global box office, becoming the fourth highest-grossing movie of the year after just 12 days in thea
body:
“The Odyssey” has surpassed $700 million at the global box office, becoming the fourth highest-grossing movie of the year after just 12 days in theaters.

	Christopher Nolan‘s Greek epic has generated $320.5 million domestically and $407.4 million overseas, bringing worldwide ticket sales to $727.9 million. Hollywood’s top three releases of 2026 are June’s “Toy Story 5” ($1.02 billion) and April’s “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” ($1.001 billion) and “Michael” ($1.001 billion). In the coming week, “The Odyssey” will join those films in the billion-dollar club, a remarkable feat that underscores Nolan’s ability to transform his movies into cultural events.
	

	These ticket sales are all the more impressive considering that “The Odyssey” has yet to open in China, the world’s second-biggest moviegoing market. The country is rolling out the red-carpet treatment for the film, which is expected to land on nearly 800 Imax screens — and across thousands of standard auditoriums on Aug. 14. 


	Even with outsized competition from Sony and Marvel’s adventure “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which debuts on Friday and is primed to score one of the biggest openings of all time, “The Odyssey” is expected to remain a force at the box office. It could earn as much as $50 million to $60 million in its third weekend of release, a tally that most adult-skewing dramas would be lucky to earn in their debuts these days.

	“The Odyssey” cost $250 million, marking Nolan’s most expensive film to date. It’ll soon be his most commercially successful, too. It’s primed to overtake “The Dark Knight” ($1.008 billion) and 2012’s “The Dark Knight Rises” ($1.08 billion) as the director’s highest-grossing film of all time. 
	

	Adapted from Homer’s 3,000-year-old epic poem and starring Matt Damon as the Greek king Odysseus, “The Odyssey” has been a major draw in Imax. As the first feature shot entirely with Imax cameras, it’s been sold out in those formats for weeks. So far, Imax has contributed $140 million of the film’s global ticket sales. It’s the company’s second-fastest title (after “Avengers: Endgame”) to surpass the $100 million mark, having done so in just 10 days.

schema.headline: ‘The Odyssey’ Surpasses $700 Million Globally After 12 Days in Theaters

title: Bruce Campbell to Bring ‘Ernie & Emma’ on Nationwide Alamo Drafthouse Tour This Fall (EXCLUSIVE) – Film News in Brief
description:
Bruce Campbell is set to bring his new independent film, “Ernie & Emma,” to Alamo Drafthouse screens this fall.

	The nationwide tour will feature C
body:
Bruce Campbell is set to bring his new independent film, “Ernie & Emma,” to Alamo Drafthouse screens this fall.

	The nationwide tour will feature Campbell in-person, beginning Friday, Sept. 4 in Los Angeles before stops in San Francisco, New York City, Texas, Washington, D.C., North Carolina, Virginia and more cities through Nov. 14. The romantic comedy “Ernie & Emma,” which Campbell directed, wrote, produced and starred in, follows a small-town salesman who goes on a road trip across Oregon to honor his late wife through a “meticulous list of instructions she leaves behind,” according to an official synopsis.
	

	“It’s incredibly special to share this film with audiences across the nation. Getting to bring it directly to communities and experience those conversations in real time is the reason you make something like this in the first place,” Campbell said in a statement. “I’m going to start these screenings with one question: ‘How many people here have lost a loved one? Raise your hand. Every hand is going to go up. That’s why I believe this movie connects with everyone. Loss is universal, and so is the challenge of finding your way forward.”


	In addition to his acting work in “The Evil Dead” trilogy and “Spider-Man 2,” Campbell previously directed “My Name is Bruce,” “Make Love! The Bruce Campbell Way” and “Man with the Screaming Brain.”
	
		Wednesday, July 29	
	
		Cosm and Warner Bros. Pictures Set Shared Reality Release of ‘It’	

	Cosm and Warner Bros. Pictures announced “It” will premiere in shared reality at Cosm venues on Aug. 28.
	

	Cosm will utilize its 87-foot-diameter, 12K+ LED domes and fulldome production technology to transport guests to Derry, Maine. Intensified sound design and dynamic environments will supplement the jump scares in the horror film, which premiered in 2017 and quickly became the highest grossing horror film.

	“Over the past year, we’ve seen experiential cinema in Shared Reality bring to life a fresh, exciting way for fans to interact with – and enter the worlds of – their favorite films,” said Alexis Scalice, vice president of business development and entertainment at Cosm.

	“It” marks the fourth entry in Cosm’s film portfolio, along with “The Matrix,” “Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory” and “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone.”

	“It” will premiere at Cosm Los Angeles, Dallas and Atlanta on Aug. 28, and at Cosm Detroit at a later date.
	
		Tuesday, July 28	
	
		Byron Allen’s Freestyle Digital Media Picks Up Jeff Ryan’s Golf Crime Comedy ‘Mooch’	

	Freestyle Digital Media has acquired the golf crime comedy “Mooch,” written by, directed by and starring Jeff Ryan. “Mooch” will debut on digital platforms starting Aug. 14. Ryan, who retains theatrical rights through is First-Names Films, will release the film in a national roadshow of one-night screenings developed in partnership with Emo Nite, featuring live performances from its soundtrack artists. 

	“The rollout reimagines the theatrical experience for the ‘Mooch’ audience: part screening, part concert, part reunion for a generation raised on Warped Tour,” the filmmakers said in a statement. The ensemble cast includes Scott Cohen, Katerina Tannenbaum, Geneva Carr, Molly Brown, Ashby Gentry, Will Chase, Louis Cancelmi Olli Haaskivii, Ian Dolley, Natalie Roy and Oscar Williams. 

	Featuring an original emo soundtrack, “Mooch” tells the story of Shane, the oldest caddy at his local golf club, who takes on the job of digging up dirt for a charismatic New Jersey nightclub owner. 
	
		Monday, July 27	
	
		CSA Announces 2026-27 Board of Directors and Dates, Venues and Timeline for 42nd Annual Artios Awards	

	The Casting Society announced its newly elected Board of Directors for the 2026-27 term, as well as the date, venues and voting timeline for the 42nd annual Artios Awards. 
	

	The Artios Awards will be Feb. 18, 2027, with events in Beverly Hills, New York City and London. The awards recognize excellence in casting in film, television, commercials and theater.

	The 2026-27 Board of Directors includes Destiny Lilly, Elizabeth Berra, Matthew Glasner, Sujotta Pace, Danielle Pretsfelder Demchick, Devon Brady, Jazzy Collins, Wendy Kurtzman, Asjai Lou, Gayle Pillsbury, Rachel Reiss, Erica A. Hart, Felicia Joseph, Tiffany Mak, Becca McCracken and Dustin Presley.

	The 2026-27 CSA Global Chapter Board of Governors includes Cassandra Han, Dave Bennett, Sien Josephine Teijssen, Kei Kawamura, Mawuko Kuadzi and Maria Lainas.

	Phase 1 submissions for the Artios Awards are open Aug. 3-13, with nominees announced Oct. 7. Phase 2 submissions are open Oct. 26-Nov. 5, with nominees announced Dec. 16.

schema.headline: Bruce Campbell to Bring ‘Ernie & Emma’ on Nationwide Alamo Drafthouse Tour This Fall (EXCLUSIVE) – Film News in Brief

title: Ewan McGregor and Alan Cumming to Lead Scottish Stage Adaptation of Harry Macqueen’s Gay Romantic Drama ‘Supernova’
description: Two of Scotland’s best known faces from cinema and TV are set to tread the boards together for the first time and at a theater close to their home t
body:
Two of Scotland’s best known faces from cinema and TV are set to tread the boards together for the first time and at a theater close to their home towns. 

	“Trainspotting” legend Ewan McGregor and “The Traitors” favorite Alan Cumming will take the lead in the stage adaptation of Harry Macqueen’s highly acclaimed 2020 romantic drama “Supernova,” which starred Colin Firth and Stanley Tucci and was shortlisted for two BAFTA awards, including best film.
	

	The production of “Supernova” will run during the summer of 2027 at the Pitlochry Festival Theatre, where Cumming currently serves as artistic director.


	Marking his stage debut as a playwright, Macqueen has adapted his own film, while John Tiffany is set to direct. 

	“Supernova” follows Sam and Tusker, a loving couple who have been together for 20 years. But since Tusker’s early-onset dementia diagnosis their lives have changed forever. Now, the two are setting off on a road trip chasing the memories they’ve built, visiting the people they love and dodging the future they can’t outrun. As per the synopsis, “Supernova” is a “searing examination of what we are willing to do for the people we love.”

	Director Tiffany will reunite with his longtime collaborator, the movement director Steven Hoggart, the two having been behind the likes of “Harry Potter and the Cursed Child,” “Black Watch” and, more recently, “Once.” Meanwhile, Jamie Harrison, who worked on “Stranger Things: The First Shadow” in both the West End and Broadway, will serve as designer.

	“I am so excited to welcome Ewan, a fellow Perthshire home boy, to Pitlochry Festival Theatre for this extraordinary theatre event,” said Cumming. “Harry Macqueen has adapted his beautiful film, and John Tiffany and Steven Hoggett (fresh from their Pitlochry Festival Theatre triumph with ‘Once’) join forces with the theatrical wizard Jamie Harrison to create an evening of true magic. A love story, a treatise on life and death itself and a visual feast — with two Scottish laddies at its heart. What more could you want?!”
	

	Added McGregor: “I am so delighted to be working at Pitlochry Festival Theatre next summer on the beautiful ‘Supernova’ with my old friend Alan. I have been very moved by the work so far on the text by Harry Macqueen who is adapting his own screenplay. We are going to be discovering this story with the amazing team of John Tiffany, Jamie Harrison and Steven Hoggett and it’s going to be quite something to throw myself into this role with such an extraordinary group of visionaries. I can’t wait to get started and to bring this piece to the stage. I look forward to seeing you all there!”

	The Pitlochry Festival Theatre production of “Supernova” will run from July 24 until August 21 2007.

schema.headline: Ewan McGregor and Alan Cumming to Lead Scottish Stage Adaptation of Harry Macqueen’s Gay Romantic Drama ‘Supernova’

title: Ozzy Osbourne Haunted Experience Is Headed to Universal Studios’ Halloween Horror Nights
description: Universal Studios’ Halloween Horror Nights is set to pay tribute to Ozzy Osbourne with an original haunted house dubbed “Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Da
body:
Universal Studios’ Halloween Horror Nights is set to pay tribute to Ozzy Osbourne with an original haunted house dubbed “Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness.”

	As part of the experience, guests will be able to climb aboard the “Crazy Train” for a terrifying trip through his disturbing world of rock ‘n’ roll.

	Developed as a living horror movie through the lens of Halloween Horror Nights, this non-traditional memorial to Osbourne, who died in 2025, will span 45 years, transporting guests on a twisted journey though the artist’s solo career in unique experiences across both coasts.
	

	At Universal Studios Hollywood, the haunted house transports fans to where it all began, in Birmingham, England, home to John Michael “Ozzy” Osbourne. Starting with “Crazy Train,” Osbourne’s most famous song, guests will travel through time from his early childhood to the Osbourne Asylum, inspired by his iconic album Diary of a Madman. As they weave through the decades, the unique iterations of Ozzy’s persona will come to life, from Madman Ozzy and Werewolf Ozzy to the Prince of Darkness, the moniker he earned in the 1970s.


	Music from Osbourne’s solo albums including “The Blizzard of Ozz,” “Diary of a Madman,” “Bark at the Moon,” “No More Tears,” “Scream” and “Ordinary Man” will all be featured.

	In a joint statement, Sharon and Jack Osbourne said, “Ozzy never stopped pushing boundaries, and he loved anything that gave fans a new way to experience his music and the worlds he created.” They added, “Halloween Horror Nights has done an incredible job bringing that spirit to life. Walking through these haunted houses, you’ll recognize so many moments inspired by his music and imagination. It’s a wonderful tribute to Ozzy, and we hope fans have as much fun experiencing it as he would have had seeing it come together.”
	

	At Universal Orlando, Halloween Horror Nights guests will venture through ancient ruins and foreboding dungeons before boarding the “Crazy Train” for a twisted ride into a realm inspired by the covers of his fan-favorite albums, “Diary of a Madman,” “Bark at the Moon,” “The Ultimate Sin” and” Black Rain.” Ruled by the Prince of Darkness, this fantastical world draws from the heavier sound and sinister imagery that defined the later years of Ozzy’s career, transforming that creative evolution into a horrific journey through his unmistakably twisted imagination.

	“Ozzy Osbourne didn’t just help define heavy metal—he created a cultural phenomenon that has influenced generations of music, art and horror,” said John Murdy, Executive Producer of Halloween Horror Nights at Universal Studios Hollywood. “We previously had the privilege of collaborating with Ozzy, and this new haunted house is an opportunity to honor his extraordinary solo career. Inspired by all 13 of his albums, guests will journey through the dark, surreal worlds that fueled his music and cemented his legacy as the one and only Prince of Darkness.”

	Mike Aiello, Senior Director of Entertainment Creative Development at Universal Orlando Resort added, “We are honored to collaborate with the Osbourne family to create a unique haunted house that celebrates the legacy of Ozzy Osbourne.” He went on to say, “It was important for us to create an authentic experience that brings Ozzy’s creativity and personality to life in an eerily immersive new way. Fans will discover so many meaningful details, including a few Easter eggs, as they navigate memorable dark and twisted moments inspired by his iconic musical career.”

	New limited-release merchandise inspired by the “Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness” haunted houses, including a T-shirt and an Ozzy acrylic figure which can be added to the separately sold Infernal Carnival collectible display, are now available at Universal Orlando Resort and Universal Studios Hollywood.

	As previously announced, “Sinners,” “Evil Dead Burn” and “Stranger Things” have also been added to the lineup.

	Halloween Horror Nights runs select nights at Universal Orlando Resort, beginning Aug. 28 through Nov. 1, and at Universal Studios Hollywood from Sept. 3 through Nov. 1. Additional haunted houses and event content will be revealed soon. Tickets are on sale at HalloweenHorrorNights.com.
	

	Watch the teaser below.

schema.headline: Ozzy Osbourne Haunted Experience Is Headed to Universal Studios’ Halloween Horror Nights

title: ‘Tony’ Review: Dominic Sessa Gives His First Movie-Star Performance in Matt Johnson’s Tasty Biopic About the Young Anthony Bourdain
description: Watching a biopic, or reviewing one, I can’t say that I’ve ever spent much time wondering what the subject of the movie might think of it. Would Jam
body:
Watching a biopic, or reviewing one, I can’t say that I’ve ever spent much time wondering what the subject of the movie might think of it. Would James Brown have liked “Get On Up,” the superb 2014 drama about him? He would probably have found something in it to gripe about. Elton John lovingly endorsed “Rocketman,” the 2019 film about him that I thought was a laughably inauthentic piece of junk.

	But as I watched “Tony,” Matt Johnson’s drama about the young Anthony Bourdain and the summer he spent in Provincetown working in a restaurant kitchen for the first time, I couldn’t help but wonder what Bourdain himself would have made of the movie. How could you not wonder? He was too opinionated, too no bullshit, too much of a movie fanatic, too much the kind of guy who would greet a film about him not by feeling flattered but by pissing all over it because it had missed the real story. To me, if an Anthony Bourdain biopic can’t clear the bar called “Bourdain would have liked it,” it’s probably not a good movie.
	

	“Tony” clears that bar. It’s true to what happened to Bourdain in 1975, when he was a restless 19-year-old college student spending the summer in Provincetown. The movie is structured as a romance, and some of it is fictionalized, but it’s true to the person he was and was becoming: a charmer, a troublemaker, a middle-class Jersey refugee with some serious demons, an aspiring writer with an extraordinary gift of gab, a sweet kid, a hustler, and an asshole. “Tony” has been framed as the origin story of how Anthony Bourdain became Anthony Bourdain. But one of the many things that Matt Johnson, the director of “Blackberry” and “Nirvana The Band the Show the Movie,” understands is that Anthony — or, as he called himself then, Tony — already was Anthony Bourdain.
	

	In the opening scene, he’s trying to impress a panel of English professors at Vassar College, pitching them the novel he wants to write, so that he can be chosen for a summer writing fellowship. He’s giving them a spiel, but it’s brilliant, and you feel the electricity of his talent — his subversive and funny desire to stir the pot. We can already hear his voice, which sounds like the voice of a flaked-out post-counterculture brainiac bohemian crossed with Howard Stern.

	The movie is based on several early chapters from “Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly,” the extraordinary my-life-in-restaurants memoir, published in 2000, that made Bourdain an overnight celebrity. For some of us, his voice in that book was transcendent — the way he was so cathartically honest about the life he’d led, his pursuit of pleasure and appetite and escape (to the point that he became a functional heroin addict), and his unprecedented evocation of what it’s really like to work in a restaurant kitchen, which he depicted as a rough-and-tumble sweatshop of discipline and ball-busting and perfectionistic culinary fetishism. He made you want to be there, in the heat, on the line; he also made you think at times, There but for the grace of God…

	Bourdain tapped into our collective obsessive belief in food as something holy, but he also showed you the truth of that world as if it were a movie: the funk and the flavor, the addiction and abuse, the cold-beer-at-midnight glory. Even before he became the preeminent television rock star of celebrity chefs, Bourdain captured the seductive rock ‘n’ roll of life in the kitchen; he was a hipster in chef’s whites who could see through everyone in the room. In “Tony,” he’s a lot more innocent, but the story is built around a terrifically layered irony. The movie is all about how Tony knows, in his bones, that he wants to be a writer, but discovers that he was meant to be a chef. And yet…he really was meant to be a writer. He falls in love with restaurant work, but what he’s falling for isn’t just the food — it’s the drama.

	To me, one of the most pleasurable things in movies is that moment when you see an actor become a movie star. That’s what happens to Dominic Sessa in “Tony.” I don’t care if the film is a summer indie smash or not (though it deserves to be) — it shows you that Sessa has the goods, in the way his breakout performance in the likable but overly soft faux-’70s movie “The Holdovers” did not. What a movie star needs (among other qualities) is anger, and Sessa plays Tony as an eager, voluble, simmering bad boy who is playing out his inner turmoil in the real world. His Tony, tall under a curly ’70s moptop and sideburns, has the look of a hungry dog. At his family’s home, when he’s waiting to hear whether he’s been chosen for the writing fellowship, we see the dynamic that has made him the outspoken yet emotionally bottled-up soul he is. His mother, Gladys (Dagmara Domińczyk), is brilliant and exacting, but she’s also the chief critic of everyone around her. She has given Tony his voice of judgment, which he turns on the world but also, compulsively, on himself.
	

	Sessa gives Tony the charisma of anger, and he also shows us the youthful confusion that sent him spiraling to Provincetown. Back at Vassar, at a bar, he hits on Nancy, played by Emilia Jones with a toughness as radiant as it is savvy. He’s already half in love with her, and his mixture of awkwardness and aggression has an effect on the audience, as it does on her. In a way it’s cringe, yet you can’t take your eyes off him. Tony is a mess, but he’s sly, with the magnetism of someone who can talk his way past shame.

	When he doesn’t get the fellowship, it leaves him in a rage of discontent. He’s an entitled son-of-a-bitch, but his egomania is part of what’s going to take him far. That, and his ability to make stuff up. He’s a compulsive liar, and he decides, on a WTF whim, to head to Provincetown, where Nancy is spending the summer, and to basically spend his time there stalking her. He tells everyone there that he’s got the writing fellowship, which for Tony is a class-snob thing; it makes him feel worthy. But he has no fellowship, and no money. The first night, seated at a bar, he spends the last of his cash on a tray of raw oysters and half a dozen beers (he tries to woo the bartender by explaining how eating an oyster as a kid in France changed his life — a formative Bourdain anecdote), and he makes a drunken spectacle of himself. He gets thrown out on his ass by the owner.

	But the next day he swings by to apologize, and the owner, who is known only as Chef (Antonio Banderas), takes pity on him and gives him a job washing dishes, as well as a place to crash (the hammock on his back porch, where he awakens Tony each morning by dousing him in a bucket of seawater). Provincetown was a less chic place then than it is now, and Tony doesn’t see working in the cramped, messy kitchen of a bare-bones seafood restaurant called the Flagship — they have four things on the menu, notably lobster rolls — as a ticket to anything. He thinks what he’s doing is lowly. The film introduces us to the screw-loose types who work there, although they’re never portrayed as cartoons: the blitzed slob Stavros (Stavros Halkias) and Sal (Leo Woodall), a ladies’ man so aggro he’s a complete sociopath (he carves a shard of wood out of the wall as a trophy each time he scores, which is often — it’s the hook-up ’70s). The movie follows them to late-night house parties, but the real action is in the kitchen, where they fight their hangovers with morning lines of coke, and where Johnson stages the combustible goings-on with an existential, at times violent spontaneity that takes these scenes to a level of unwashed kitchen-sink reality that I’ve never felt “The Bear” quite got to.
	

	The beauty of “Tony” is that it doesn’t make anything feel predetermined. It’s the story of an old-school American summer — those months when a college kid like Tony, doing a job because he needs a job, has the drifting freedom to fall into random experiences, because that’s the enchantment of being in a Cape Cod beach town in 1975. Tony ambles around, gets into fights, does hard drugs, fruitlessly pursues Nancy (who has a boyfriend in the pizza shop she works at), sinks into the scuzzpit of washing dishes, then graduates to food prep, all under the tutelage of Chef, the foodie task-master.

	Through it all, Tony doesn’t realize that this is his real school; that’s the way the summer that changes your life works. “Tony” has an enchanted spirit of discovery that reminded me of “Adventureland,” Greg Mottola’s winsome gem about working at an amusement park in the summer of ’87. Like that film, it’s a nostalgic dream that’s alive to the moment. More than that, though, “Tony” has the organic flow and humanity, and the craft so light it’s invisible, of a Richard Linklater film. It might be the best Linklater movie Linklater never made.  

	It’s Chef who presides over the controlled chaos, and Antonio Banderas invests him with a delectable blend of gentleness and cutthroat authority, as well as an undercurrent of mystery. Who is this man who shucks oysters as if preparing the Eucharist? Banderas gives a fantastic performance, showing us how Chef becomes Tony’s mentor by being everything he’s not: calm, contained, devoted to the task at hand, attuned to something higher. At Tony learns on one privileged day in the otherwise empty restaurant, the man even makes his own ketchup! Yet Tony awakens something in Chef too — an ambition he left behind. The movie shows you that there’s a Zen to the kitchen, and that all of life can grow out of that. As Tony’s troubled soul comes to the fore, acted out in ways both big and small, what’s revealed is that though he wants to be a writer, he believes in nothing. “Tony” is about how he finds himself by crawling out of himself. The kitchen wounds him, heals him, and becomes his crucible of faith.

schema.headline: ‘Tony’ Review: Dominic Sessa Gives His First Movie-Star Performance in Matt Johnson’s Tasty Biopic About the Young Anthony Bourdain

title: Sundance Teases New Theaters in Boulder, Expanded Competition Slots as Industry Heads to Colorado for ‘Orientation’
description: Hollywood hasn’t begun packing for the fall festivals in Venice, Telluride and Toronto, but the Sundance Film Festival has dropped in with a reminde
body:
Hollywood hasn’t begun packing for the fall festivals in Venice, Telluride and Toronto, but the Sundance Film Festival has dropped in with a reminder that January is around the corner.

	On Wednesday, leadership at Sundance sent out a mid-year update on the fest’s seismic move from Park City, Utah, to the Colorado mountain town of Boulder, setting the stage for state-of-the-art movie theaters, expanded competition slots and a much larger swath of ground to cover for industry types and filmmakers.
	

	“In the new footprint, our venues are all within about a 2-mile radius,” wrote festival director and head of public programming Eugene Hernandez in a missive, pointing to key venues that will house the festival’s trove of indie films. 


	That includes the University of Colorado Boulder’s Macky Auditorium, the Chautauqua Auditorium, Boulder Theater and the honest-to-God multiplex Cinemark Century (any Sundance veteran will be confounded by watching screenings in an actual modern movie theater, not a makeshift public building or school auditorium).

	To call the location change an adjustment might be an understatement. To combat the shock, Sundance has been hosting “industry orientations,” as one source put it, for major stakeholders on the ground. Agents, artists, PR teams and more have been shuttling to Boulder to get the lay of the land. They’re also getting more opportunities for Sundance glory. 

	Hernandez announced that four central competition categories — U.S. Dramatic, World Cinema Dramatic, U.S. Documentary, and World Cinema Documentary — will grow to 12 films from 10. Other sections, including Premieres, NEXT, Midnight, Family Matinee, and more, will also expand.
	

	Read expanded points from Sundance’s mid-year update:

	Save the Dates

	The 2027 Sundance Film Festival will take place January 21–31, in Boulder, Colorado. World premieres will be held Thursday, January 21, to Tuesday, January 26 — Festivalgoers will be part of the first audiences ever to see brand-new films, episodic projects, and more. Throughout the entire run of the Festival additional showings of the 2027 program will continue until the Festival wraps.

	Our annual Festival gala will take place on Friday, January 22. This event raises vital funds to support independent artists through our year-round programs.

	For those joining us outside of Colorado, anywhere across the country, we’ll again offer at-home online screenings from Thursday, January 28, to Sunday, January 31, offering films in our five competition sections, including NEXT. Films from other sections in our lineup can also choose to participate in the online Festival program for limited audiences. Press and industry will have online access to the at-home program for the professional community beginning one day earlier on Wednesday, January 27.

	An Expanded Program

	In this moment when artists are seeking more support, we’re thrilled that Boulder allows us to expand our program size and connect even more films with Sundance Film Festival audiences.

	In 2027, our four central competition categories — U.S. Dramatic, World Cinema Dramatic, U.S. Documentary, and World Cinema Documentary — will grow to 12 films each. Other sections, including Premieres, NEXT, Midnight, Family Matinee, and more, will also expand.

	This undercurrent of expansion runs throughout the entire Festival. Our Offscreen (formerly known as Beyond Film) programming slate — Cinema Café, The Big Conversation, Power of Story — will be expanding our signature talks and thoughtful events with artists and colleagues to include live podcast recordings and more.

	In September, we’ll share more information on Fest passes, ticket packages, and single film tickets so you can decide the best way to experience everything the Festival has to offer. Passes and packages go on sale in October, and single film tickets in early January. Stay tuned for more details on the ticketing products available as well as the 2027 lineup, which will be announced in December. Be sure to create a Festival account and opt in to receive email communications to get the latest updates.
	

	If you want to get early access to Festival passes and packages, become a Sundance Institute Member or donor. Besides sustaining our year-round artist programs and initiatives, supporters get early access to ticket sales, discounts on merchandise (which you can use to pick up some more 2026 gear right now!), and more.

	New Frontier FLUX

	For the last two years, New Frontier — our dynamic, cutting-edge program at the intersection of art, cinematic storytelling, and emerging technologies — has been on pause to evaluate the rapid changes in our media landscape. Determined to stay with our community as we face the uncertainty of our times, New Frontier will return to the 2027 edition of the Festival as New Frontier FLUX to activate inside the massive fluctuations of our biodigital realities.

	Committed to experimentation and interdisciplinary practice, New Frontier FLUX radically pushes at formal cinematic boundaries to champion and cultivate maverick, independent storytelling. As we plant roots in Boulder, a community that holds a deep, long-standing love of experimentation and exploration, we are excited to have found a home for this courageous section of the Festival.

	Exciting Additions to Festival Awards

	Toward the end of the Festival, we honor the projects and artists that have graced our screens for nine days, celebrating their accomplishments and dedication to creating culture-shifting, unique stories. The 2027 Sundance Film Festival jury and audience awards will be announced on Friday, January 29.

	For the first time, we’re thrilled to welcome the International Federation of Film Critics (FIPRESCI) to the Sundance Film Festival. FIPRESCI will establish their own jury who will select winners for Best Debut Narrative in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition and Best Debut Documentary within the World Cinema Documentary Competition. FIPRESCI will present these awards during our awards ceremony. This partnership is a great way to welcome our international community as we kick off our Festival in Boulder.

	In addition, the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences has acknowledged the works of our global filmmakers by making the Sundance Film Festival an Academy Awards–qualifying Festival for World Cinema Grand Jury Prize winners, Documentary and Dramatic. Simply, this means that our World Cinema Grand Jury Prize winners will automatically qualify for the upcoming Oscars in the International Feature Film Category. This change is so exciting for all of us at the Institute as it continues to uphold the mission of supporting and highlighting groundbreaking artists from around the globe.
	

	Speaking of Hard Work

	Our Festival has a proud history of working with volunteers throughout our venues and programs, and this year is no different. We will be welcoming over 2,000 volunteers from across the world and around the corner to bring our Festival to life. Volunteer applications will open on our website August 31, 2026, for anyone who may want to get involved!

	Boulder Is Full of Options

	Naturally, the questions we hear most from our Festival community are about our transportation and lodging. A new location brings new logistics to learn and new neighborhoods to explore. One of our favorite things about Boulder is how easy it is to get around, whether walking, riding a scooter or e-bike, or taking advantage of the city’s robust local transportation system with bus routes that seamlessly reach all our venues. Regional buses from around the area, including Denver and the airport, connect directly into this Boulder system.

	Another thing about our new Fest home that I’ve fallen in love with is the sheer convenience for our audiences and artists — from locally owned and award-winning places to eat (over 100 in the heart of Boulder, 400 in the city!), to spots to grab a drink, to shops for last-minute necessities and gifts, there are countless options for how to shape your days in Boulder! Visit Boulder will be providing easily accessible, interactive guides on where to eat by each theater to help attendees make quick decisions between films. From high-quality grab-and-go options to a MICHELIN-star meal, and everything in between, Boulder has it all!

	Wondering where to stay? The Lodging section of our How to Fest guide has information on hotels and short-term rentals in and around Boulder and surrounding areas, as well as info on transportation for those who want to experience more of Colorado by staying in Denver or nearby commutable areas. This site will continue to be updated as more inventory is added throughout the year at lodging.sundance.org.

	If you are coming from overseas, good news: There are over 30 direct international flight routes to Denver International Airport in January, including flights from London, Mexico City, Tokyo, Toronto, and more.

	There is something magical about experiencing stories with people you don’t know. These experiences bring us together, and being a part of this community creates the memories we take home with us. Our whole team is working hand in hand every day to build the new foundation for our Festival with our incredible partners in Boulder.
	

	I can’t wait for us all to kick off this next chapter of the Sundance Film Festival together in Boulder, Colorado, in January, because it wouldn’t be the Sundance Film Festival without you.

	Eugene

schema.headline: Sundance Teases New Theaters in Boulder, Expanded Competition Slots as Industry Heads to Colorado for ‘Orientation’

title: AMC NASCAR Series ‘Thunder Road’ Casts ‘Silo’ Star Shane McRae (EXLCUSIVE)
description:

	The series, which is produce
body:
Shane McRae is the latest addition to the upcoming AMC drama series “Thunder Road,” Variety has learned exclusively. 

	The series, which is produced in a partnership between AMC and NASCAR, is set in the world of stock car racing with Dennis Quaid set for the lead role. It was greenlit at AMC in April with plans to launch it in 2027 on AMC and AMC+. 

	The logline for the show describes it as a “multi-generational saga of the fictional Whitlock family, whose legacy in stock car racing is as deep as the family’s ties to the southern hill country roots that shaped them.” 
	

	Quaid will play racing legend Duane Whitlock, while McRae will appear in the series regular role of Scooter Jakes. Scooter is said to be “whip-lean, weathered, and predator-calm. Scooter Jakes is a veteran of the NASCAR circuit. He’s a cornerstone of Whitlock Racing Team as crew chief to Trey in the legendary #28 car — and as one of the only people Duane (Quaid) wants alongside him at crunch time.” 


	Along with Quaid and McRae, the cast currently includes Michael Rooker, Maggie Grace, Matt Barr, West Duchovny, Chase Stokes, and Devon Allman. 

	McRae currently stars in the Apple TV drama “Silo” in the role of Knox and has been with the show since its first season. He also recently appeared in the critically acclaimed FX series “The Lowdown” and will return for its second season. His other TV credits include “Paradise Lost” for Spectrum Originals, “Alaska Daily” at ABC, “Sneaky Pete” at Amazon, and “The Following” at Fox. He has appeared in films like “The Help,” “Still Alice,” and “The Adjustment Bureau.”  
	

	He is repped by Gersh. 

	John Fusco created “Thunder Road” and serves as executive producer. Taylor Elmore is attached to serve as executive producer and showrunner. Cliff Roberts of Syndicate Entertainment executive produces along with Mark L. Smith and NASCAR Studios’ Tim Clark and John Dahl. Gladys Cheng is a producer. AMC Studios and NASCAR Studios produce.

title: ‘The Master and Margarita’ Adaptation Gets Long-Awaited U.S. Theatrical Release After Legal Battle (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Michael Lockshin’s Russian-language adaptation of Mikhail Bulgakov’s “The Master and Margarita” is finally getting a long-awaited U.S. theatrical re
body:
Michael Lockshin’s Russian-language adaptation of Mikhail Bulgakov’s “The Master and Margarita” is finally getting a long-awaited U.S. theatrical release.

	Following a lengthy battle, Luminosity Pictures are rolling the movie out Stateside from Sept. 18, Variety can confirm.

	Based on Bulgakov’s seminal, semi-autobiographical work, “The Master and Margarita” follows the story of a writer in 1930s Moscow. After being censored, he writes a new novel in which the Devil appears to wreak havoc on those who have wronged the author. It stars August Diehl, Yevgeny Tsyganov, Yuliya Snigir and Claes Bang, among others.
	

	Lockshin completed the movie just before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. By the time it was ready for release in Jan. 2024, its themes of censorship and resistance were deemed too controversial by the Kremlin, which criticized both Lockshin, who has been public in his support for Ukraine, and the movie and insisted on removal of scenes.


	Despite that, Lockshin’s work saw huge box office in the country, becoming the highest-grossing 18+ release in Russian history. International distribution was delayed after sanctions against Russia saw the film caught up in complex legal wrangling, intensified by competing claims by self-proclaimed rights-holders to Bulgakov’s original text.

	Those issues have now been resolved to the extent the film, which has had releases in Germany, Austria, Sweden and Italy, among other territories, is finally set to hit U.S. screens. Lumonsity will release Lockshin’s restored director’s cut.

	“When we started working on the film, we couldn’t have foreseen that a story about censorship and standing up for truth set in the 1930s would turn out to be so much about the present – in Russia and beyond it,” said Lockshin. “I’m very grateful to the people who came on board and pushed forward to get this film out despite the geopolitical and legal issues.”
	

	Luminosity Pictures co-founder said Peter Hoffman said: “For more than 25 years, my companies have sought to finance and distribute a film adaptation of the extraordinary novel ‘The Master and Margarita.’ When colleagues gave me the opportunity to view Michael Lockshin’s brilliant adaptation of this literary masterpiece, I immediately sought out the Russian producers to bring this unique film to audiences outside the Russian Federation, and they entrusted Luminosity Pictures with that opportunity. This has truly been a passion project for me, and everyone involved has poured their hearts into honoring Bulgakov’s remarkable novel. We hope audiences are swept away by its romance, imagination, and timeless themes, and discover why this extraordinary story has captivated readers around the world for generations.”

	Lockshin directs from a screenplay he co-wrote with Roman Kantor. He is repped by 42’s Josh Varney and Peter Dealbert, and by Gang, Tyre, Ramer, Brown & Passman.

	The film is produced by Ruben Dishdishyan, Leonard Blavatnik, Igor Tolstunov and Anatoly Akimenko.

	Luminosity was founded in 2023. As well as “The Master and Margarita” the company is representing upcoming rom-com “A Murder Uncorked,” starring Emma Roberts and Lucas Bravo, and prison siege thriller “Eleven Days” with Diego Luna, Taylor Kitsch and Jason Isaacs.

title: EFD Studios Names José Miguel Álvarez Ibargüengoitia CEO, EFD Studios Mexico (EXCLUSIVE)
description: EFD Studios, Latin America’s biggest film equipment rental company, has named longterm Imcine senior executive José Miguel Álvarez Ibargüengoitia as
body:
EFD Studios, Latin America’s biggest film equipment rental company, has named longterm Imcine senior executive José Miguel Álvarez Ibargüengoitia as CEO of EFD Studios Mexico.

	The appointment of Álvarez Ibargüengoitia, one of the best-known and regarded of figures on Mexico’s film industry scene, comes as EFD Studios has begun to put through an energetic expansion drive. 


	It also takes place just months after Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum and Mexican actor-producer-director Salma Hayek unveiled Feb. 15 a transferable tax credit for Mexican and international productions shooting in Mexico. Eligible spend includes post-production.    
	

	Under new global director general, Nacho Carballo, a former Madrid region audiovisual advisor who joined EFD Studios in April, EFD Studios is driving for what Carballo described to Variety as “consolidation in the national territories where we’re based – Spain, Mexico, Colombia and the U.S. – as well as international expansion.”


	“Up to now, we’ve been the No. 1 in Mexico and even Spanish-speaking America but we can’t rest on our laurels but rather renovate our studios and equipment and confront the new challenges of AI and virtual production,” he added. 

	“To do so, we must be strategically positioned. Signing José Miguel is very, very important. He’s one of Mexico’s stars.”

	“This is an important moment for the Mexican industry with a new incentive, significant state funds for production and a film industry open for international co-production which is recognized in the world,” said Álvarez Ibargüengoitia.
	

	“The strengthening of the industry and AV ecosystem in Mexico and Latin America also has to do with companies like EFD Studios, sectorial leaders which know the business, know to be allies or partners with production teams, bet on powerful stories and have the capacity to grow in Mexico taking its industry to other States in the country,” he added.  

	In Mexico, Álvarez Ibargüengoitia will oversee an operation which prides itself on its advanced tech services for top players in the country. On “Pedro Páramo,” one of the highest-profile Netflix series in Mexico, for instance, EFD supplied not only mobile lighting and grip equipment but also ARRI’s M-series lights, SkyPanels, power generators, and a Fisher Dolly 11. 

	At Imcine, Álvarez Ibargüengoitia served as MD of international promotion over 2013-17 before becoming its director of film production (2017-26) and also technical co-ordinator (2019-26). He can be expected to use his vast network of contacts to attract both international shoots to Mexico and Mexican productions to EFD Studios. 

	EFD Studios will continue its training and refresher programs for technicians. “There’s an explosion of productions and the challenge is to have enough trained and specialised technicians to work on them,” Carballo said. The Studios will also create a consultancy for producers to access the new tax credits whose structure is little known, especially among younger and new producers, said Carballo. 

	“[EFD Studios Group President] Georgina Terán’s bet is on cinema in Spanish. It’s a bet to defend our roots, language, the quality of our cinema. We’re over 600 million speaking the same language  and we have a lot of stories to tell. It’s a bet on Hispano-American talent and new creators,” said Carballo.

title: Marisa Tomei, Matthew Broderick, Amy Brenneman and More Present Staged Reading of ‘The Big Chill’ for the Center at West Park (EXCLUSIVE)
description: The Center at West Park, a New York City nonprofit community, arts and culture hub, will return to East Hampton to present a one-night-only staged r
body:
The Center at West Park, a New York City nonprofit community, arts and culture hub, will return to East Hampton to present a one-night-only staged reading of the “The Big Chill.” 

	The ensemble will feature Oscar-winner Marisa Tomei (“My Cousin Vinny,” “The Wrestler”), Tony Award-winner Matthew Broderick (“The Producers”), Emmy Award-nominee Amy Brenneman (“Judging Amy”), Spencer Garrett (“Once Upon a Time in Hollywood”), Drama Desk Award-winner Frederick Weller (“In Plain Sight”), Ilana Levine (“Tanner ’88”) and New York City Public Advocate Jumaane D. Williams, with additional all-star cast members to be announced in the coming weeks. David Saint will direct. The performance will be followed by a talkback featuring the cast, creative team, and special guests.
	

	“The Big Chill” is a beloved 1983 dramedy about a group of college pals who regroup in middle age for the funeral of a friend. It was co-written and directed by Lawrence Kasdan and starred Kevin Kline, Glenn Close, Jeff Goldblum, Tom Berenger, William Hurt, Mary Kay Place, Meg Tilly, and JoBeth Williams. Barbara Benedek co-wrote the film, which was nominated for three Oscars. 


	The reading will be held on Monday, August 31st at 7:00 p.m. at Guild Hall, located at 158Main Street, East Hampton, NY 11937. The Center at West Park is located on Manhattan’s Upper West Side and serves all five boroughs of New York City. The performance will have a single showing followed by a talkback with the cast and creative team. 

	Last year’s staged reading of “All the President’s Men” at Guild Hall, which featured Alec Baldwin, AndyCohen, Maddie Corman, Robert Downey Jr., Corey Hawkins, Nathan Lane, Kenneth Lonergan, JulianneMoore, Gwyneth Paltrow, Wendell Pierce, Mark Ruffalo, J. Smith-Cameron, New York City PublicAdvocate Jumaane D. Williams, and Ramy Youssef. “It’s a tremendous privilege for The Center at West Park to serve audiences across New York and to continue our summer performance tradition in East Hampton at Guild Hall,” said Debby Hirshman, executive director of The Center at West Park. “After the incredible response to last summer’s staged reading of ‘All the President’s Men,’ we’re thrilled to return with ‘The Big Chill’ — a timeless film whose humor, heart, and unforgettable characters continue to resonate. We’re especially excited to welcome an extraordinary cast, including Marisa Tomei, Matthew Broderick, Amy Brenneman, Spencer Garrett, Frederick Weller, Ilana Levine, and Jumaane D. Williams. We look forward to sharing another unforgettable evening of storytelling with audiences at Guild Hall.”

	This reading is presented with the support of Columbia Pictures. This performance of “The Big Chill” is produced by Julianne Hoffenberg alongside Hirshman and Madelyn Paquette, resident producer at The Center at West Park.

	Tickets for the one night-only performance range from $1,000 to $10,000 and can be purchased atthe center’s website.

            As we reported, four women recently accused the Oscar winner of sexually assaulting them or threatening to sexually assault them when they were teenagers.

            Six other women also spoke about alleged experiences with Leto in the BBC documentary "Jared Leto: Hollywood's Dark Secret." The outlet says all of the alleged incidents occurred between 2002 and 2016, when Leto was in his 30s and 40s.
      
    
            He is now 54 years old ... and tells us the accusations are categorically false.

title: Dashcam Captures Terrifying Moment Truck Collides With Tractor-Trailer
description:
Crazy Collision
                          Truck T-Boned & Semi Smashed
body:
Crazy Collision
                          Truck T-Boned & Semi Smashed
                          ... On Video!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 29, 2026
                            9:00 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Three cars were completely totaled when a truck collided with a tractor-trailer ... and the insane accident was caught on video.
      
    
            Another semi was waiting to turn at the intersection of W Avenue and Highway 3 in Iowa on Monday, and you can see the tractor-trailer coming down the road on the dashcam.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As it approaches the intersection, a Dodge Ram comes into frame from the road on the right, barreling towards the stop sign and blowing right through it.
      

            As you can see ... the truck completely cuts off the semi, smashing the front of the cab and getting T-boned in the process.
      
    
            According to the Fayette County Sheriff's Office, the trucks collided with a Chevy Impala sitting at a stop sign off camera, noting all three vehicles are "a total loss."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The truck's driver, his passenger, and the semi's driver were all taken to Community Memorial Hospital in Sumner, the sheriff's office says.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The extent of any injuries is unclear, and the authorities didn't mention how the sedan's driver is doing.
      
    
            The crash investigation is ongoing.
